designs.title: No.
designs.why: The joke lands in one look: the cat bats the full stop off 'No.' like a toy, and the sidelong, unimpressed face is the best drawing on the sheet. Confident brush line, the two rules hold the lockup together, it sits at a good size on the back and reads well as white ink on black. What keeps it from $50 territory is the texture inside the letters. The uneven white dashes look like random scratches, not deliberate tabby stripes, and they clash with the fine diagonal hatching on the tail. Two textures fight, and the heavy 'NO' gets busy right where it needs to be graphic. The whiskers and fine hatch lines are close to the limit for one-ink screen print and may break or fill in.
designs.fix: Rework the stripes in the letters into a few deliberate tabby bands, consistent in weight, spacing and slight curve, and make them match the tail's marking (or drop the letter texture and set 'NO' solid). Thicken the hairline whiskers and hatching a little so they hold in print.
